issues.legal_issue: A revenue-record entry made pursuant to an alleged correction order, without other evidence of title, is insufficient to establish ownership of land.
material_facts: The claimants sought a declaration of ownership and possession of the disputed land.
The original revenue record showed the land in the name of a former intermediary and later in the name of the State.
The alleged order directing correction of the record was not produced; the claimants relied on the resulting entry in the register.
The claimants identified no other document or evidence supporting their title.
issues.conclusion: The courts below erred in declaring the claimants’ title on the basis of the correction and resulting revenue entry. The appeal was allowed, the judgments and decrees were set aside, and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: An entry in revenue records does not create or extinguish title and cannot, by itself, support a declaration of ownership. No earlier cases or statutory provisions were relied on for this principle.

rule.if: declaratory_title_suit and revenue_entry_is_only_title_evidence and correction_order_not_produced and no_other_title_evidence

predicates.declaratory_title_suit: The claimants brought a civil suit seeking a declaration that they owned land.
predicates.revenue_entry_is_only_title_evidence: The claimants relied on an entry in a revenue record as their evidence of ownership.
predicates.correction_order_not_produced: The claimants did not produce the order said to have directed the correction of the revenue record.
predicates.no_other_title_evidence: The claimants identified no other evidence supporting their asserted ownership.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks a declaration of ownership and the claimant relies only on a revenue entry, does not produce the order said to have caused it, and offers no other title evidence, the title claim is not established.
